title: What Pharmacy Technicians Do
description: Pharmacy technicians are the pharmacist's essential partner: they receive and enter prescriptions, count and label medications, manage inventory, process insurance claims, compound non-sterile preparations, and serve patients at pickup. The pharmacist verifies everything and counsels — the technician makes the whole system move.
key_points: Receive, enter, fill, label — the dispensing pipeline
Pharmacist verifies all; technician powers the flow
how_it_works: Receive prescriptions and enter data accurately
Fill and label under pharmacist supervision
Manage inventory and serve patients at pickup
requirements: High school diploma; accredited training program or on-the-job training
PTCB (CPhT) or NHA (ExCPT) certification in most states
State registration or licensure where required
Background check and drug screening
Continuing education for certification renewal
standards: The five rights: right patient, drug, dose, route, time
Double-check high-alert medications
Accurate data entry and label verification
HIPAA privacy for all patient information
safety: Never dispense without pharmacist verification
Separate look-alike/sound-alike drugs (LASA) on shelves
Cleanroom garbing and aseptic technique for sterile compounding
Report errors through the pharmacy's safety system without fear
troubleshooting: Insurance rejection: check BIN/PCN, prior auth, formulary alternatives
Unclear prescription: never guess — clarify with prescriber via pharmacist
Short inventory: check wholesaler, transfer, or partial fill options
Angry patient at pickup: listen, verify, escalate to pharmacist
citations: Pharmacy Technician Certification Board guidance; American Society of Health-System Pharmacists resources; pharmacy practice references.
provenance: Public trade knowledge drawn from pharmacy technician education, professional association guidance, and pharmacy practice references. Real, fact-checked records.
